papers.title: Decoupling candidate dual AGN from chance superpositions in the GOTHIC survey via a deep-learning framework
papers.abstract: Dual active galactic nuclei (DAGN) mark a critical phase in the evolution of merging galaxies and the pairing of supermassive black holes, yet they remain difficult to identify in large imaging surveys because of projection effects and limited spatial resolution. Compact foreground stars and unresolved substructure can mimic dual nuclei through chance superposition, complicating automated detection. We revisit the 46,061 galaxies flagged but rejected as DAGN candidates by the GOTHIC pipeline, primarily because the two nuclei fell within the SDSS fibre aperture or exceeded its separation threshold. We train a supervised deep-learning framework based on the YOLOv11 oriented-bounding-box architecture on annotated SDSS imaging to separate genuine dual nuclei from foreground stellar contaminants and other spurious alignments. The final model attains a validation precision of 0.919, recall of 0.905, and $F_1$ of 0.912, and yields 29,605 dual-nucleus candidates after removing star-dominated and blended detections. Structured visual inspection indicates that $54.5$--$62\%$ are consistent with genuine dual nuclei, implying $\sim(1.4$--$1.8)\times10^{4}$ plausible systems. Cross-calibrating the YOLO separation against the deterministic GOTHIC centroid measurement and restricting to the compact regime ($d \le 6.87''$) gives a conservative subset of $\sim 13{,}672$ candidates, reaching calibrated separations of $\sim 0.56''$. Spectroscopy of the most compact ($\le 1$ kpc) systems shows spectra dominated by stellar absorption, with no resolved double-peaked emission, so confirmation requires higher-resolution follow-up. The catalogue is a statistically refined list of candidates, not confirmed DAGN. Nonetheless, deep-learning detection substantially reduces contamination and expands the plausible DAGN census.

papers.title: Variance of relative entropy over random states
papers.abstract: Average relative entropy over major generic random states is recently studied. In this work, the investigation is extended by deriving the variances of relative entropy over the Hilbert--Schmidt and Bures--Hall ensembles, which characterize its fluctuations around the average value. Exact results for the variances of relative entropy between independent states drawn from the same ensemble and from two different ensembles are obtained. These results further indicate that the average relative entropy is typical in the considered limiting regimes. In addition to the matrix-level calculations similar to the average relative entropy, eigenvalue correlation functions of the ensembles are involved in the variance computations through the use of zonal polynomials.

papers.title: New time-periodic solutions to the cubic conformal wave equation on $\mathbb{S}^{3}$: I Spherical symmetry
papers.abstract: We present a rigorous construction of novel time-periodic solutions to the radially symmetric cubic conformal wave equation on the Einstein cylinder $\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{S}^{3}$. Their existence, hinted by the earlier numerical studies (arXiv:2504.10513), complements prior results on Cantor sets of infinitesimally small solutions. Our proof, based on the contraction principle, requires extensive computations that are performed on a computer by the means of rational arithmetic. We are able to significantly reduce their amount by a thorough analysis of the inverse of the associated linear operator, leading to sharper analytical bounds, as well as introduction of simplified versions of certain relevant operators. We provide examples of three solutions with specific frequency; however, our techniques and tools can be directly adapted to prove the existence of other solutions conjectured in (arXiv:2504.10513).

papers.title: Corner Regularity and Asymptotics for the Two-Dimensional Radiation Transport Equation
papers.abstract: The regularity of solutions to the two-dimensional radiation transport equation plays a central role in understanding the behavior of scalar flux near geometric corners. In a previous study of Kaper's corner singularity problem, the physical transport kernel was decomposed into its principal inverse-distance singularity and a lower-order remainder, reducing the corner asymptotic analysis to the question of whether the scalar flux possesses sufficient continuity to justify differentiation of the associated singular potential. The required regularity, however, remained unresolved. In this paper, we establish a sharp modulus-of-continuity estimate for the scalar flux generated by the physical transport kernel and prove the estimate $\omega_{\phi}(h)=O\!\left(h\log(D/h)\right)$, which implies Dini continuity. This estimate yields absolute convergence of the fluctuation term arising in the differentiated principal potential and permits a rigorous differentiation formula for transport solutions. Using this regularity framework, we derive the fixed-angle asymptotic behavior of the scalar flux and its first derivatives near a rectangular corner. For every fixed interior ray, the gradient exhibits logarithmic growth, while the scalar flux admits an $r\log(1/r)$ correction with an explicitly identified coefficient determined by the corner values of the flux and source. The analysis shows that a rectangular corner does not generate a singularity stronger than the logarithmic first-derivative singularity already present in smooth-boundary transport theory. Numerical calculations on benchmark problems are consistent with the theoretical predictions. These results provide a rigorous resolution of the regularity issue underlying Kaper's corner singularity problem and establish a mathematical framework for corner asymptotics in two-dimensional radiation transport.

papers.title: The Two-Dimensional Narrow Escape Problem with Deterministic Initial Condition: Mean Escape Time and Escape location probabilities
papers.abstract: This paper presents a rigorous asymptotic analysis of the two-dimensional narrow escape problem for a Brownian particle initiated at a deterministic position x. While we address the mean escape time, the main novelty lies in our derivation of the asymptotic escape distribution. We derive explicit asymptotic formulas that characterize the dependence of the escape behavior on the relative configuration of the starting point and the window centers. These results remain valid as the starting position approaches the boundary windows and include refined error estimates. The formulas are obtained with two independent methods, each of them having their own interest. A central feature of this work is the rigorous treatment of the underlying mixed boundary value problems in the absence of a contact angle at the escape window boundaries. By leveraging recent results on the maximal regularity of the gradient of the solutions of such mixed boundary value problems, we ensure the analytical validity of our approach despite the inherent loss of regularity of these solutions at the escape window boundaries. Finally, we apply these general results to provide a full sharp asymptotic equivalents for regimes where window sizes scale at specific relative rates.

papers.title: Symmetries and Higher-Form Connections in Derived Differential Geometry
papers.abstract: We introduce a general definition of higher-form connections on principal $\infty$-bundles in differential geometry. These connections are built as infinitesimal parallel transports and thus satisfy the fake-curvature condition. We achieve this by developing the formal differentiation and integration of maps from smooth manifolds to derived stacks with sufficient deformation theory. That allows us to introduce the Atiyah $L_\infty$-algebroid of a principal $\infty$-bundle and establish its global sections as the $L_\infty$-algebra of the derived higher symmetry group of the bundle. We define the space of $p$-form connections on an $\infty$-bundle as the space of order $p$ splittings of its Atiyah $L_\infty$-algebroid. This can be cast equivalently as lifting the classifying map of a bundle on a manifold to the order $p$ truncation of the de Rham stack of the manifold. We demonstrate that our new concept of derived geometric $p$-form connections recovers the known notion of connections on higher U(1)-bundles defined via \v{C}ech-Deligne differential cocycles. We further relate the $L_\infty$-algebras of derived higher symmetries of higher U(1)-bundles and higher Courant algebroids. Some applications in higher gauge theory and in supergravity are mentioned.

papers.title: Christoffel transformations of symmetric $d$-connections and gap probability recurrences
papers.abstract: We study the Christoffel transformation $w(x)\mapsto x^2w(x)$ of an even discrete weight. For the associated orthogonal polynomial ensembles on squared nodes $y=x^2$, ratios of moment determinants relate the largest-particle distributions and transfer exact gap probability recurrences between the ensembles. For positive weights satisfying the stated moment and support assumptions, this comparison requires no Pearson condition. The transformation is realized by elementary bundle modifications at zero and infinity on $\mathbb P^1$. When the original weight has Pearson ratio $d(-z-1)/d(z)$ with $\mathrm{deg}\; d=1,2$, these modifications conjugate cutoff dynamics on common stable loci of symmetric $d$-connections under the stated geometric hypotheses. The transformed recurrence coefficients are expressed explicitly as rational functions of spectral coordinates. On the unit lattice, a local recurrence formula applies to rational symmetric Pearson ratios of arbitrary degree, including outside these charts, whenever its local hypotheses hold.

papers.title: Bounded compositions and products of chains, or bi(s)nomials everywhere from de Moivre's formula to spin multiplicities and constant-sum codes
papers.abstract: How many ways are there to select $k$ objects from $n$ types when type $i$ is available in only $s_{i}$ copies? For equal bounds, this is de Moivre's problem of obtaining a prescribed total with $n$ dice, now a textbook application of the principle of inclusion-exclusion. For arbitrary bounds, the answer is encoded by the rank polynomial $\prod_{i=1}^{n}(1+x+\cdots+x^{s_{i}})$. Its coefficients enumerate bounded compositions and submultisets, give, after normalization, the probability mass function of a sum of independent discrete uniform random variables, and are the weight multiplicities of a tensor product of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ representations. Most of these interpretations are classical but dispersed; here we place them in a common notation and document their provenance. A complement involution proves symmetry and boundary identities. For arbitrary bounds, lower-half first differences give both symmetric-chain starts and mixed-spin multiplicities, and the chain-length and irreducible-dimension profiles agree. Convolution gives log-concavity and the central mode. For equal bounds with fixed $s \geq 1$ and even $ns$, local expansions give central asymptotics with explicit $1/n$ and $1/n^{2}$ corrections for the coefficient and its first difference. A Poisson limit gives the first boundary crossover of these differences at scale $k \sim \lambda n^{s/(s+1)}$, with factor $e^{-\alpha\lambda^{s+1}}$ when the proportion of bounds equal to the fixed minimum $s \geq 1$ tends to $\alpha>0$. Central first differences include the $s$-Catalan numbers, themselves Littlewood-Richardson coefficients; central layers yield maximum-size constant-sum codebooks for hash-based signatures. Under the polynomial binomial convention, the full inclusion-exclusion transform vanishes, and the omitted terms sum to the negative of the number of bounded compositions.

papers.title: A generalization of Gordon's Theorem to arbitrary winding number
papers.abstract: We study minimizers of the Keplerian action functional with homogeneous potential of type $1/|u|^\alpha$ on periodic loops with fixed winding number $k \in \mathbb{Z}\setminus\{0\}$. This extends the classical theorems of Gordon and Venturelli, closing the previously open case $\alpha \in (1,2)$, $|k|\geq 2$. We show that the $k$-circular solution loses local minimality below the threshold $\alpha = 2-1/|k|^2$, and that minimizers are collision-free above $\alpha = 2-1/|k|$. Combining these results with the existence of precessing periodic orbits in between, we obtain a full classification of the minimizer in terms of $\alpha$ and $k$, which we also verify numerically for $k=2$.

papers.title: Finiteness of Dziobek central configurations in the Newtonian five-body problem
papers.abstract: We prove that, for any five fixed strictly positive masses, the Newtonian central configurations of exact affine dimension three form finitely many similarity classes. The proof uses the Dziobek equations, two constant identities, and local analysis of zeros and poles on a compact complex curve.

papers.title: Rational $S$-functions for second order ODEs with non-Liouvillian first integrals
authors: L. A. C. P. da Mota
papers.abstract: The $S$-function method for rational second order ODEs $y''=\varphi(x,y,y')$ uses $S=I_y/I_z$, attached to a first integral $I$, which satisfies a Riccati equation along the flow; it was designed for Liouvillian $I$. We study the case of rational $S$ with non-Liouvillian $I$. From any rational $g(x,y,z)$ with $g_z\neq0$ and any linear equation $A_2w''+A_1w'+A_0w=0$ with polynomial coefficients, the substitution $w'/w=g(x,y,y')$ yields a rational 2ODE whose first integral is built from two independent solutions, and $S=g_y/g_z$: the Wronskian cancels, so $S$ does not see the linear equation, and one rational $S$ is shared by equations with and without Liouvillian first integrals. Conversely, given $(\varphi,S)$, membership in this class reduces to a rational first integral of an explicit planar vector field plus a M\"obius-invariant Riccati test in $x$, which recovers the linear equation. A transfer theorem shows that $I$ is Liouvillian if and only if this equation has a Liouvillian solution, so Liouvillianity is decidable on the class by Kovacic's algorithm: a three-variable problem with no a priori degree bound is reduced to two classical ones. On nine pull-back equations of degree up to $15$, given without information on their construction, the procedure recovers the Airy equation and the Bessel equation of order zero.

papers.title: Conformal geodesics and the hyperboloid at timelike infinity
papers.abstract: A description of scattering in asymptotically flat spacetimes that includes both radiation and massive asymptotic states requires control of the relation between null and timelike infinity. Motivated by this problem, we use the properties of conformal geodesics to construct an extended representation of timelike infinity in Minkowski spacetime. The construction exploits the fact that every non-null metric geodesic in an Einstein spacetime is, up to an explicit local reparametrisation, a conformal geodesic. It replaces the point $i^+$ by a hyperboloidal boundary $\mathcal{H}^+$ meeting future null infinity $\mathscr{I}^+$ at a corner $\mathcal{C}^{+}$, while fixing the location of $\mathscr{I}^+$ in the associated conformal Gaussian gauge. In this gauge, we derive the equations governing massless scalar and spin-$2$ fields. In particular, we obtain a transport equation for the scalar field along future null infinity and analyse the asymptotic behaviour of its spherical-harmonic modes near timelike infinity. We also derive the explicit massless spin-$2$ equations in this gauge. Finally, we examine the relation to projective extensions and to the hyperbolic base of the extended Carrollian space $\mathrm{Ti}$. Our results provide a geometric framework for studying the connection between late-time and null asymptotics which is a prerequisite for scattering constructions relevant to flat space holography.

papers.title: Perfect t-Embeddings of Uniformly Weighted Generalized Tower Graphs
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study sequences of perfect t-embeddings of a uniformly weighted family of graphs we call generalized tower graphs. We show that the embeddings of these graphs satisfy certain technical assumptions, in particular, the rigidity assumption of Berggren-Nicoletti-Russkikh. As a result, we confirm the convergence of the gradients of the height function fluctuations of these graphs to those of the Gaussian free field.

papers.title: Stochastic stability of master--slave synchronization for a class of PDEs with Burgers-type nonlinearity
papers.abstract: Master--slave synchronization reconstructs the evolving state of a reference (or master) system by continuously correcting a second system, the slave, using observations of the master. In applications, the observations are often contaminated by noise, so the corrections injected into the slave are themselves uncertain. In this paper we aim at quantifying the effect of noisy observations on master--slave synchronization for a family of evolution equations that combine a quadratic transport term with a polynomial linear differential operator. The family includes the Burgers, Kuramoto--Sivashinsky, Kawahara, Benney--Lin and Nikolaevskiy equations, among others. Under periodic boundary conditions, a Fourier--Galerkin approximation of order $K$ yields a finite-dimensional master--slave system in which white observation noise of intensity $\sigma$ is modeled through an It\^o stochastic differential equation. In this framework, we first establish local exponential stability of noiseless synchronization for sufficiently strong scalar coupling. Then we compare the stochastic synchronization error with its noiseless counterpart resulting from the same initial slave state, isolating in this way the effect of noise. Assuming bounded reference paths, the mean-square deviation between the noiseless and noisy synchronization errors is $\mathcal O(\sigma^2)$ on finite time intervals. Under additional regularity assumptions, we also bound the error between the finite-resolution stochastic slave model and the infinite-dimensional deterministic master field, explicitly separating spectral approximation error, deterministic synchronization error and observation noise. Numerical experiments for the Kawahara and Nikolaevskiy equations confirm the predicted noise scaling.

papers.title: Soft elasticity of soft shells
papers.abstract: Soft modes of a shell are one-parameter families of non-trivial deformations that preserve the elastic energy. We identify all soft modes of the soft shells described by the variational theory of put forward by Sonnet and Virga (2025). They are seen to be strictly connected with the Bonnet families, a special class of solutions to the problem posited by Bonnet, who asked whether there exist non-trivial isometries that preserve the mean curvature. Differential geometry deems as equivalent all surfaces in one and the same Bonnet family, but continuum mechanics is interested more specifically in soft deformation modes and the shapes they traverse, as they may describe ways to ignite fluctuations of soft shells that ideally require no energy to be activated. We give a general criterion for the existence of soft modes and a method to construct them based on a cascade of path integrations. We apply both criterion and method to some exemplary cases.

papers.title: Strongly non-linear continuous model for wave propagation in 2D granular media: derivation and hyperbolicity analysis
papers.abstract: In this work, we develop a nonlinear continuum model for wave propagation in two-dimensional granular materials, building on key ideas from Nesterenko's work. Starting from the Hertzian contact law and neglecting contact friction, we derive an effective continuum description through homogenization, assuming spherical, monodisperse grains, local periodicity, and the Cauchy--Born hypothesis. The resulting strain-gradient model depends on both the first and second gradients of the displacement field. We analyse the hyperbolicity of the leading-order system through its eigenvalues and eigenvectors, establishing conditions for hyperbolicity within a restricted deformation domain. The model is solved using an explicit finite-volume method to investigate gravitational settling and wave propagation. We derive analytical expressions for the longitudinal and transverse wave speeds and highlight their dependence on depth. Finally, the predictions of the continuum model are compared with existing discrete-element simulations. This formulation allows several extensions, including more complex packing geometries, contact laws, and large-deformation regimes in which the contact network can evolve.

papers.title: Quasideterminants and differential realizations of W-algebras
papers.abstract: In this work, we study the Hamiltonian reduction, used in constructing finite rectangular $W$-algebras, of the big-cell differential realization of $\mathfrak{gl}_{np}$. We establish an intrinsic factorization of the reduced differential realization, identifying its Yangian action with the coproduct action on a tensor product of $n$ evaluation differential realizations of $\mathfrak{gl}_p$. Corner quasideterminants provide the essential noncommutative mechanism through which Hamiltonian reduction transforms the higher-rank differential realization into a factorized lower-rank Yangian action.

papers.title: Spin Toda systems and N-point spherical Whittaker functions
papers.abstract: We define and study a spin version of the open Toda integrable system, using the Iwasawa decomposition of a connected split real Lie group. We study spherical Whittaker functions as solutions of the spin Toda system. We also construct their N-point version and find the corresponding factorisation of the Casimir element, which yields asymptotic boundary KZB type equations.

papers.title: Averages of traces and ratios of characteristic polynomials of random unitary matrices
papers.abstract: In this work we explore the extent to which the Ratios Theorem for averages over $U(N)$, with respect to Haar measure, of ratios of characteristic polynomials can be used to evaluate averages of traces of unitary matrices. We derive concrete expressions for all averages involving up to 4 traces, valid for any matrix size, $N$. We also calculate the so-called zero-swap and one-swap contributions to an average with any number of traces, which amounts to determining general trace moments in a range double the size of the renowned result of Diaconis and Shahshahani. The expression is tractable enough to use in applications, for example to determine the parameter range where certain trace averages assume negative values.

papers.title: On Trace Averages and Sharp Asymptotics for Powers of Haar-Unitary Matrices
papers.abstract: For a Haar-distributed matrix $U \in U(N)$, Rains's power-map theorem represents the spectrum of $U^m$, $m \in \mathbb{N}$, as a superposition of independent lower-dimensional CUE spectra. We determine how this exact decomposition appears in trace moments and in sharp Gaussian and Poisson limit laws. For averages of mixed trace products, a Charlier--Ewens convolution separates the stable Wick term from its full finite-$N$ correction. A Fredholm factorisation gives sharp total-variation asymptotics for the normalised trace in four regimes, from fixed powers to $m\geq N$. For a fixed trace power $p$, coherent summation of the leading Laguerre correction yields the exact factor $e^{2/p}$. At the mean-spacing scale, we obtain a sharp Poisson limit for the unfolded spectrum of $U^m$ on a fixed interval as $N, m \rightarrow \infty$; its first-order correction, obtained via the second Charlier polynomial, quantifies the residual under-dispersion of local eigenvalue counts.

papers.title: The solution of the Hopfield model with Gaussian patterns
papers.abstract: We prove that the free energy of the Hopfield model with Gaussian patterns has a thermodynamic limit at every load $\alpha$ and temperature $T$, and we give it as an explicit variational principle. The Hubbard--Stratonovich transformation maps the model onto $N$ Ising spins coupled to $M=\alpha N$ Gaussian hidden units, whose radius, the empirical variance of the hidden layer, is a thermodynamic variable with an entropic cost. At fixed radius the model is an Ising--spherical spin glass with Gaussian couplings, which we solve. The principle (i) reproduces the Amit-Gutfreund-Sompolinsky theory as its replica-symmetric restriction, (ii) identifies $T_g=1+\sqrt\alpha$ as the rigorous boundary of the annealed region, (iii) selects a unique spin-glass solution of the AGS equations, and (iv) gives the radius an equation of state. Moreover, (v) below $T_g$ we prove that replica symmetry is broken throughout: the instability of the AGS solution reduces to the zero-field de Almeida-Thouless condition of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model.

papers.title: Correlation-induced suppression of Granger causality and Gaussian transfer entropy
papers.abstract: In complex dynamical systems, Granger causality and transfer entropy are widely used to infer directional interactions, but they quantify a source's unique predictive contribution after conditioning and can therefore be substantially attenuated by correlation with the retained variables. Here, using our previously developed Linear Operator Causality Analysis (LOCA) framework, which measures causal response from the system propagator, we derive a relationship between predictive and operator-based causality. For a two-dimensional linear system, the fractional suppression of Granger causality equals the squared correlation between source and receiver. We generalize this result to high-dimensional systems using the source covariance remaining after conditioning and show that additional conditioning can only increase the suppression. The same covariance ordering yields a corresponding upper bound for Gaussian transfer entropy. A linearized Burgers advection chain exhibits 36.6% suppression at the convective travel-time peak, and exact nonlinear acoustic Burgers solutions show that the fitted-surrogate penalty is governed by correlation structure rather than nonlinearity and remains robust to sensor noise after operator debiasing. Applied to resting-state fMRI from the Human Connectome Project (80 brain regions, 8 functional networks, 10 subjects), the single-lag Granger causality measure falls 39.4% below the operator response when conditioning only on the receiver and 73.0% when conditioning on the receiver and all other retained variables. The framework provides a quantitative bridge between predictive and operator-based causal measures in high-dimensional dynamical systems.

papers.title: Ideal interaction dynamics of defects and background fields in condensed matter
papers.abstract: While defect dynamics in condensed matter systems is widely studied and several methods are available to track the defect position over time, the formulation of dynamical models for the coupled evolution of both defect and background field quantities seems to be more challenging. Yet, the overall behavior of a system containing moving defects is strongly influenced by this defect-field interaction. Here, we propose a modeling framework for the conservative coupled evolution of the defect density and the background fields upon focusing on two relevant cases of study: the Gross-Pitaevskii theory of quantum fluids and the Ericksen-Leslie model of nematic liquid crystals. To achieve the coupled evolution, we combine the Euler-Poincar\'e variational setting of continuum dynamics with the gauge theory of topological defects. While the latter allows us to overcome certain ambiguities in definition of the defect density, the Euler-Poincar\'e method provides a unified modeling approach in the absence of defect reconnection.

papers.title: M5-brane source charges, Chern--Connes pairings and noncommutative compactifications
papers.abstract: We formulate a source-adapted Chern--Connes description of M5-brane magnetic charge in physically motivated noncommutative and quotient linking sectors. The starting point is the local codimension-five geometry of an M5-brane source: the magnetic charge is measured on a four-dimensional link. In the smooth local model the link is the ordinary four-sphere, and the pairing reduces to the standard flux integral of the M-theory four-form field strength. The construction is motivated by the published even-codimensional Noncommutative Foliation Invariant (NCFI for short), where Connes' transverse fundamental cyclic cocycle is paired with an even transverse-geometric \(K\)-class. For an M5-brane the relevant codimension is odd, so the required odd \(K\)-class is supplied instead by the boundary map of the source/linking extension. Noncommutative or groupoid algebras are used only when they arise from physical mechanisms: Matrix/M-theory compactification on noncommutative tori, reduction to D-branes in background \(B\)-fields, large \(C\)-field M5 limits, or quotient/orbifold source links. The result is a topological charge formula, not a derivation of the full M5-brane dynamics or of the complete M-theory action.

papers.title: Free energy fluctuations of symmetric perceptron models up to and including criticality
papers.abstract: We study the free energy fluctuations of spherical and Ising perceptron models with general even activations. These include the symmetric binary perceptron, the $U$-perceptron, and the bipartite Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model. Our main result is a Gaussian CLT for the free energy that holds both in the ``high-temperature'' interior of a second moment RS regime and on its ``critical'' boundary. At criticality, the CLT has scale $(\frac{\log N}{6})^{1/2}$, which matches the free energy fluctuations of the critical Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model and suggests this scaling is universal. The proof shows that the perceptron model's free energy fluctuations are explained, up to an additive $o(1)$ error with high probability, by those of a corresponding spherical Hopfield model, and that this relation persists even at criticality. This proof strategy builds on a critical reweighted moment method developed by the first and third authors \cite{du2026fluctuations} to identify the critical fluctuations of the SK free energy, which links these fluctuations to the spectral edge spacing of the disorder.

papers.title: Probabilistic representation and Monte Carlo method for nonlinear Dirac equations
papers.abstract: Dirac equations describe the relativistic evolution of quantum particles. Using the point-process stochastic calculus of piecewise-deterministic Markov processes (PDMPs) on general state spaces, which naturally allows additional Feynman-Kac potentials, we develop a probabilistic representation for the nonlinear Dirac equations in $1+1$ spacetime dimension with cubic nonlinearity and $L_\infty$-type problem data using a multi-type branching telegraph process together with both continuous and jump-type multiplicative functionals. Our main theorem leads to a classification result which, when applied to the specific Soler model, gives a sharp finite-time admissibility of the probabilistic representation. By extending the one-step representation to a multi-step, time-marching representation using an analytically-derived a priori $L_\infty$ estimate, we observe a ``local probabilistic representation, but global PDE well-posedness" phenomenon. We proceed to propose a time-marching Monte Carlo algorithm as a global numerical solver for the Soler system with a rigorous convergence proof and establish an additional stability result on the PDE side. Finally, while the underlying process parameters do not affect the validity of the probabilistic representation, we observe their potential for variance reduction in the Monte Carlo methods.

papers.title: Can Spontaneous Time-Translation Symmetry Breaking Be Quantized Without Explicit Branches?
papers.abstract: Can classically branched dynamics associated with spontaneous time-translation-symmetry breaking be quantized without explicitly retaining the branches of the Hamiltonian? We investigate this question using a reduced phase space. formulation in which the Hamiltonian is single-valued, while the critical structure of the classical Legendre map is encoded in a singular, momentum-dependent symplectic geometry. Quantization of the reduced Poisson algebra yields a deformed position-momentum commutator whose singularities determine distinct regular momentum sectors. Using the positive measure induced by the reduced symplectic structure, we identify a bounded central sector and two unbounded outer sectors. In the central sector, states with vanishing mean momentum obey a nonzero lower bound on position uncertainty, subject to the operator-domain assumptions of the representation. We further identify a possible field-theoretic connection with k-essence, where nonlinear scalar-field kinetics can produce finite-velocity degeneracies of the Legendre map. The relationship between the resulting reduced quantum description and branch-matching quantization remains unresolved and requires a comparison of the corresponding Hilbert spaces and operator domains.

papers.title: Performing a Quantum Subroutine Using Cluster States
papers.abstract: Quantum subroutines, like their classical counterparts, serve as essential components of larger algorithms. They can be realized using gate based architectures or measurement based quantum computation (MBQC), where computation proceeds through adaptive measurements on highly entangled cluster states. In this work, we implement a phase oracle as a reusable subroutine within the MBQC framework using experimentally feasible cluster states. Unlike prior demonstrations of Grover's algorithm in MBQC that omit explicit oracle construction, our approach provides a transparent formulation of the oracle subroutine, including its measurement patterns, byproduct correlations, density-matrix simulations, and corresponding MBQC measurement circuits.

papers.title: Existence and Absence of Spin-Glass Phases on Migdal--Kadanoff Hierarchical Lattices: A Complete Classification
papers.abstract: We consider the Ising spin-glass model on Migdal--Kadanoff (MK) hierarchical lattices, characterized by the fractal dimension $d=1+\log s/\log b$, where $s$ and $b$ denote the number of parallel branches and the number of bonds in series within each branch, respectively. For independent Gaussian couplings, we rigorously establish a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of finite-temperature spin-glass order for arbitrary integers $b,s\ge2$. We prove that a finite-temperature spin-glass phase exists whenever \[ \frac{b}{\sqrt{s}} \left( \frac{b\sqrt{s(s-1)}}{bs-1} \right)^{s-1}<1. \] In particular, this condition holds for all three-dimensional MK hierarchical lattices ($d=3$, or equivalently $s=b^2$), regardless of the choice of $b$. Conversely, we prove the absence of finite-temperature spin-glass order for fractal dimensions $d<1+\log17/\log6\approx2.58$, as well as in the large-$b$ limit for any fixed $d<3$. In the intermediate regime $1+\log17/\log6\le d<3$, we provide a finite-step procedure to determine the presence or absence of spin-glass order, which depends on $b$ and $s$. Our results provide a complete characterization of finite-temperature spin-glass order on MK hierarchical lattices.

papers.title: Commuting Families of Flag Quasideterminants in Reflection Equation Algebras of Type A
papers.abstract: We consider a family of northeastern antidiagonal quasideterminants associated with the successive blocks of the generating matrix of a reflection equation (RE) algebra of type $A_{n-1}$. Our main result proves the conjecture on their pairwise commutativity formulated earlier. The proof uses the triangular realization of the RE algebra in a quantum enveloping algebra and the flag property of quasideterminants. We also discuss the interpretation of these elements in terms of quantum cluster coordinates and their possible connection with generalized Toda systems.
